content: Before going to the king uninvited, what did Queen Esther ask the Jews in Susa to do?
explanation: She needed God's help. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me.” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: How many days did Queen Esther ask the Jews to fast before she went to the king?
explanation: Esther and her maidens fasted too. “Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Knowing it was against the law to see the king uninvited, what did Esther say?
options: The king will never see me
explanation: Esther was willing to risk her life for her people. “And if I perish, I perish!” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Mordecai told Esther that perhaps she had become queen for what?
explanation: God had placed her where she could help. “And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14, BSB)

content: When Queen Esther came to the king uninvited, what did he hold out to her?
explanation: It meant she was welcome and would live. “The king extended the gold scepter in his hand toward Esther” (Esther 5:2, BSB)

content: When Esther came before the king, how much did he offer to give her?
explanation: She had found favor in his sight. “Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you.” (Esther 5:3, BSB)

content: On the night King Xerxes could not sleep, what did he have read to him?
explanation: There he learned that Mordecai had saved his life. “so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.” (Esther 6:1, BSB)

content: Whom did King Xerxes order Haman to honor with the royal robe and horse?
explanation: Haman had to honor the man he hated. “Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew” (Esther 6:10, BSB)

content: At her banquet, whom did Queen Esther name as the enemy of her people?
explanation: Haman stood in terror before the king and queen. “The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!” (Esther 7:6, BSB)

content: In the story of Queen Esther, what happened to Haman in the end?
options: He was hanged on his own gallows
explanation: The gallows he built for Mordecai was used for him. “So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.” (Esther 7:10, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, which king reigned over 127 provinces?
explanation: He ruled a huge empire. “This is what happened in the days of Xerxes, who reigned over 127 provinces” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which queen refused to come when King Xerxes called her?
explanation: The king was furious with her. “Queen Vashti, however, refused to come at the king’s command” (Esther 1:12, BSB)

content: Who raised Esther after her parents died?
explanation: Mordecai took her in as his own daughter. “And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: What was Queen Esther's Hebrew name?
explanation: Esther was her Persian name. “Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther)” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: Why did King Xerxes make Esther his queen?
options: He loved her more than all others
She won a contest of strength
explanation: She found favor in his sight. “And the king loved Esther more than all the other women” (Esther 2:17, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of a plot to kill King Xerxes, whom did he tell?
explanation: Esther told the king on Mordecai's behalf. “he reported it to Queen Esther” (Esther 2:22, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, why was Haman angry with Mordecai?
options: Mordecai would not bow to him
explanation: Everyone else at the king's gate bowed down. “But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.” (Esther 3:2, BSB)

content: Because of his anger at Mordecai, whom did Haman plan to destroy?
options: All the Jews in the kingdom
explanation: He hated Mordecai's whole people. “he sought to destroy all of Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes.” (Esther 3:6, BSB)

content: What did Haman cast to choose the day to destroy the Jews?
explanation: The feast of Purim is named after it. “the Pur (that is, the lot) was cast before Haman” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of Haman's plot against the Jews, what did he put on?
explanation: He mourned loudly in the city. “he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes” (Esther 4:1, BSB)

content: When King Xerxes learned Mordecai had saved his life, what reward had Mordecai been given?
explanation: So the king decided to honor him. ““Nothing has been done for him,” replied the king’s attendants.” (Esther 6:3, BSB)

content: After Haman's death, who received King Xerxes' signet ring?
explanation: Esther also put Mordecai over Haman's estate. “The king removed the signet ring he had recovered from Haman and presented it to Mordecai.” (Esther 8:2, BSB)

content: Which feast remembers how the Jews were saved in Queen Esther's day?
explanation: The name comes from the word Pur. “Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur.” (Esther 9:26, BSB)

content: On the third day of fasting, where did Queen Esther stand in her royal robes?
options: The inner court of the palace
explanation: The king could see her from his throne. “Esther put on her royal attire and stood in the inner court of the palace” (Esther 5:1, BSB)

content: The kingdom of Xerxes in the book of Esther stretched from India to where?
explanation: It had 127 provinces. “who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which two eunuchs plotted to kill King Xerxes?
explanation: Mordecai uncovered their plot. “Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance” (Esther 2:21, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, Haman was the son of Hammedatha and was called what?
explanation: King Xerxes raised him above all the princes. “Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, BSB)

content: In Haman's plot, in which month did the lot fall for destroying the Jews?
explanation: The lot was cast in the month of Nisan. “And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which year of King Xerxes' reign was the Pur cast against the Jews?
explanation: It was cast in the first month. “In the twelfth year of King Xerxes” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which city did Queen Esther ask the Jews to gather and fast?
explanation: Susa was where the king's palace stood. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Esther told the king she would have stayed silent if her people had only been sold as what?
explanation: But they had been sold for destruction. “If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants, I would have remained silent” (Esther 7:4, BSB)
